bullets.title: Select quotes from the works and words of Elizabeth Gilbert
The art of misdirection | Apollo Robbins
bullets.note: Apollo ([@ApolloRobbins](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/n4u05gdnnavhn43dxiv/vvc3hrhvg9g77v/aHR0cHM6Ly90d2l0dGVyLmNvbS9BcG9sbG9Sb2JiaW5z); [website](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/n4u05gdnnavhn43dxiv/m0s7h5hqe6epp9/aHR0cDovL3d3dy5hcG9sbG9yb2JiaW5zLmNvbQ==)) was first recommended to me by Tristan Harris ([@tristanharris](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/n4u05gdnnavhn43dxiv/eoaph7hl434ggw/aHR0cHM6Ly90d2l0dGVyLmNvbS90cmlzdGFuaGFycmlz)), with whom I recently recorded a podcast. The subject of that portion of the conversation was attention. This part of the video description explains how it relates: “Hailed as the greatest pickpocket in the world, Apollo Robbins studies the quirks of human behavior as he steals your watch.” It’s a fantastic demonstration of what also happens to you when you’re outmatched on social media by companies whose scientists, engineers, and business models focus on hijacking your attention.

bullets.title: Sour Grapes
bullets.note: (on** [**Amazon**](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/n4u05gdnnavhn43dxiv/z8hghnhkw2wvv8/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYW1hem9uLmNvbS9Tb3VyLUdyYXBlcy1SdWR5LUt1cm5pYXdhbi9kcC9CMDZYV0tKTjVGL3JlZj10bW1fYWl2X3N3YXRjaF8wP19lbmNvZGluZz1VVEY4JnFpZD0mc3I9)**,** [**Netflix**](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/n4u05gdnnavhn43dxiv/66ueh8h5o8oggp/aHR0cHM6Ly93d3cubmV0ZmxpeC5jb20vdGl0bGUvODAwMjk3MDg=)**, and** [**iTunes**](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/n4u05gdnnavhn43dxiv/5divh7hn7d788m/aHR0cHM6Ly9pdHVuZXMuYXBwbGUuY29tL21vdmllL3NvdXItZ3JhcGVzL2lkMTIwNDA5NTcwNT9hdD0xMGw5SVAmY3Q9UlQmdW89NQ==)**).** This film scores 95% on Rotten Tomatoes, and both the story and its cinematic telling are simply fantastic. Here’s the description: “Controversy erupts when an unassuming young man floods the American wine market with fake vintages valued in the millions, bamboozling the wine world elite, in this humorous and suspenseful tale of an ingenious con on the eve of the 2008 stock market crash.” This, much like Apollo’s video above, is a study in factors that make humans vulnerable. I’m engrossed in this subject because I have some very important decisions coming up, and I realize I’m just as vulnerable as everyone else. It’s not possible to totally prevent stupid mistakes, but I’m hoping I can improve my odds by increasing awareness of common blind spots.
